title: Minors of a product lie in both factor ideals
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, let ι, κ, ν be finite types, let A be an ι-by-κ matrix and B a κ-by-ν matrix over R, and let d be a natural number. For any matrix C, let D_d(C) be the ideal generated by det(C[rows,cols]) for injective selections rows and cols from Fin d into its row and column sets. Then D_d(AB) is contained in D_d(A) ∩ D_d(B). Empty selections have determinant 1, and an empty collection of selections generates the zero ideal.
lean_statement: ∀ {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {ι κ ν : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [Fintype ν] (A : Matrix ι κ R) (B : Matrix κ ν R) (d : ℕ), (Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ (rows : Fin d ↪ ι) (cols : Fin d ↪ ν), x = Matrix.det ((A * B).submatrix rows cols)}) ≤ (Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ (rows : Fin d ↪ ι) (cols : Fin d ↪ κ), x = Matrix.det (A.submatrix rows cols)}) ⊓ (Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ (rows : Fin d ↪ κ) (cols : Fin d ↪ ν), x = Matrix.det (B.submatrix rows cols)})
